text:
maria: quick check — we need a short plan for rolling the new service-fronting strategy (proto-first router) into prod. ops wants an easy way to see failures in the console.
chris: do you mean the UI for the rollout or the underlying routing policy? both are messy.
sasha: both. ideally the console shows per-route protocol mix, error spikes, and a suggested fallback weight. small mock: /routes/:id -> shows grpc: 40% rest: 60% + errors graph.
maria: yup. ops specifically asked: can the console auto-suggest reducing grpc weight if 5xx rate > 0.5% over 2m?
todd: auto-suggest yes, auto-act maybe no. we should surface a recommended action and a one-click rollback for canaries.
jamal: telemetry team: we have per-protocol error metrics and p95 latency. adding a derived signal (protocol_error_rate) is cheap. but we need to tag by tenant and route.
chris: tagging costs cardinality. can we sample for console-level suggestions and keep full fidelity elsewhere?
sasha: sampling + deterministic hashing by tenant should be ok. console only needs representative numbers for rollouts.
maria: decision question: do we prefer to implement graceful fallback in the edge router (proxy) or in the gateway controlplane?
todd: my vote: controlplane. keeps edge simple and enables centralized policy (quota, token billing). edge only gets routing table + weights.
jamal: controlplane also means we can instrument and expose the signals in Redwood Console more easily.
chris: downside: controlplane adds extra hop, potential latency. also need an offline fallback in case controlplane unreachable.
sasha: fallback plan: edge will have a static fallback policy: if controlplane missing, fall back to rest with known weights and degrade gracefully. this must be configurable per-tenant.
maria: what about contract/format differences? protobufs over gRPC vs JSON REST — do we transcode at gateway or require dual endpoints?
todd: transcoding at gateway is 💸 and brittle. happy path: encourage clients to use proto/gRPC. but provide a lightweight JSON bridge for external clients.
chris: we should add a translation-compat test in the rollout: for N sample requests, ensure equivalence between proto and json responses for the targeted endpoints. failure triggers canary rollback.
jamal: telemetry-wise, add a 'translation_mismatch' counter when we detect semantic differences. console shows mismatch rate.
sasha: UX: show three buttons in rollout modal: increase weight, decrease weight, pause fallback. include small reason field and linked telemetry graphs.
maria: permissions: only SRE or service-owner can flip auto-suggested actions. UI must show who triggered last change.
chris: ACLs + audit logs — we already have that for deployments, reuse same model.
todd: any objections to proto-first router + controlplane suggestions + edge static fallback?
sasha: no objections, would add a runbook snippet in the modal linking to postmortem playbooks.
jamal: pinging deploy-bot to draft canary job for this. @deploy-bot run canary job template: service-fronting-proto-canary
deploy-bot: Scheduled job template created: service-fronting-proto-canary. Cron: manual trigger. Includes metrics: p50/p95 latency by protocol, 5xx rate, translation_mismatch_rate.
maria: thanks. next steps: chris to wire telemetry signals to console, jamal to add translation_mismatch metric, sasha to produce UI mock, todd to prepare edge fallback config. will sync tomorrow 10am. :thumbsup:
